headline: Roku swings to a profit as Platform revenue keeps surging
summary_short: Roku's Q1 2026 revenue rose 22.4% y/y to $1,248.9M (down 10.5% q/q on device seasonality) as Advertising (+27%) and Subscriptions (+30%) offset a 16% Devices decline, while net income reached $85.7M ($0.57 diluted EPS) versus a $27.4M loss a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue grew 22.4% y/y to $1,248.9M (-10.5% q/q on device seasonality): Advertising +27% (video impressions +59%), Subscriptions +30% (subscriber growth plus Frndly TV and Howdy), Devices -16% (fewer player shipments). Gross profit rose 26.9% y/y to $564.9M (45% margin). GAAP operating income swung to $51.8M from a $57.7M loss; net income reached $85.7M ($0.57 diluted EPS) versus a $27.4M loss a year earlier, helped by a $13.4M gain on strategic-investment sales. Adjusted EBITDA (company-defined) was $148.4M versus $56.0M. Cash plus short-term investments totaled $2,380.2M; operating cash flow rose to $199.1M. No forward guidance was disclosed in the filing.

drivers.explanation: Advertising revenue +27% y/y on a 59% rise in video ad impressions, partly offset by a 14% lower average price per impression from product/country mix shifts.
Subscriptions revenue +30% y/y on 12% more subscriptions and a 22% higher average price per subscription, including the Frndly TV and Howdy owned-and-operated launches.
Devices revenue -16% y/y as unit volume shipped fell 15% and average selling price fell 3%, primarily on lower streaming-player sales.

Gross margin rose to 45% of revenue from 43%: Advertising margin improved to 30% from 26% of revenue; Subscriptions cost of revenue rose 50% y/y on Frndly TV/Howdy licensing costs and streaming-hours growth, partly offsetting the gain.
Swing to income from a $57.7M loss reflects revenue and gross-profit growth outpacing a modest 2% rise in total operating expenses (R&D +3%, G&A +8%, S&M -1%).
Follows the operating-income swing plus $19.7M higher other income, mainly a $13.4M gain on the sale of strategic investments.
Tracks the net-income swing to profit, partly offset by a higher weighted-average diluted share count of 151.0M versus 146.2M a year earlier.

Not separately quantified in the release; trailing-twelve-month Free Cash Flow, a company-defined non-GAAP measure, rose to $538.8M from $298.4M.

Cash fell y/y mainly on financing outflows: $100.0M of share repurchases (the buyback program began August 2025, so none occurred in Q1 2025) and $51.5M of tax payments to net-settle vested equity awards.
Equity growth reflects retained-earnings growth from the quarter's net income and additional paid-in capital, partly offset by the $100.0M of share repurchases.

Company attributes the quarter to broad Platform monetization gains (Advertising and Subscriptions both accelerating) even as it continues to trade off Devices profitability to grow Streaming Households; no forward guidance was issued in this filing.
